title: Lena and the Ledger
premise: In the winter of 1918, widowed lighthouse keeper Petra Halloran keeps her late husband's ledger of debts and favors, a record that has made her indispensable to the coastal village of Carrickmoor. When a sealed letter arrives naming the Halloran family in a smuggling plot tied to the war effort, Petra must decide whether to protect the neighbors who owe her or surrender the ledger to an investigating officer. As great storms batter the coast and the armistice negotiations stall, she races to finish repairing the lighthouse lamp workshop before it is requisitioned, discovering along the way that her husband's entries conceal his own role in the conspiracy. In the end, Petra burns the pages that would condemn the village, testifies only to what she can carry in memory, and signs the armistice night with a new identity: keeper not of the light, but of the community that survives it.
about_author: August Ashgrove is the pen name of a former archivist who spent years cataloguing maritime records from the First World War era. They write historical fiction about ordinary people whose small acts of record-keeping become acts of resistance.

chapters.title: What the Tide Brings
chapters.summary: Petra Halloran, POV. On a storm-scoured morning, Petra trims the wick, logs the weather, and reads aloud from her husband Tomas's ledger of village debts, establishing her ritual of order amid grief. A supply boat fails to arrive, hinting at wartime scarcity. Emotional beat: quiet competence masking loneliness; the lighthouse as both duty and prison.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Petra, POV. Villagers visit to settle accounts: flour owed by the O'Shea widow, mended nets for the Byrne boys. Through these transactions we meet the cast and learn how Tomas's ledger binds the community together. Petra's daughter Nell asks why they keep score at all. Emotional beat: belonging purchased through bookkeeping, and its hidden cost.

chapters.title: A Sealed Letter
chapters.summary: Petra, POV. An official envelope arrives bearing a customs seal, addressed to 'The Halloran Family.' Inside: notice that the family is named in an inquiry into contraband moving through Carrickmoor's harbor, and an officer will come within the fortnight. Petra rereads Tomas's final entries and finds gaps. Emotional beat: dread arriving on ordinary paper; the past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: Officer Quill
chapters.summary: Petra, POV. Investigating Officer Quill arrives — courteous, exhausted, more interested in going home than in justice. He gives Petra three weeks before he must file. She lies about the ledger's completeness, her first deliberate deception. Emotional beat: the vertigo of becoming someone who lies; sympathy for a man trapped by his own paperwork.

chapters.title: Nell's Questions
chapters.summary: Nell, POV. Twelve-year-old Nell explores the sea caves where she finds a crate stamped with a shipping mark matching one in her father's ledger. She hides what she found, testing her mother's stories against evidence. Emotional beat: a child's loyalty torn between parents, one dead and one present; the birth of suspicion.

chapters.title: The Workshop Still Stands
chapters.summary: Petra, POV. Requisition orders threaten the lamp workshop where Petra grinds and polishes the Fresnel lenses. She begins repairs in earnest, racing the armistice rumors — if peace is signed, the requisition may be rescinded. Quill visits, watches her work, says nothing. Emotional beat: craftsmanship as prayer; hope measured in finished work.

chapters.title: Entries in Another Hand
chapters.summary: Petra, POV. Studying the ledger by lamplight, Petra detects a second handwriting interleaved with Tomas's — coded entries of dates, tides, and initials. The smuggling ran through their own home, possibly with Tomas complicit. She confronts the O'Shea widow, who denies everything too quickly. Emotional beat: grief curdling into betrayal; the dead husband becoming a stranger.

chapters.title: Storm Warning
chapters.summary: Petra, POV. The first of the great storms hits. Petra keeps the light burning through the night while waves breach the seawall; the village shelters in the church. Quill, stranded, helps haul sandbags and sees the community's interdependence firsthand. Emotional beat: shared danger dissolving barriers; the light as promise kept to strangers at sea.

chapters.title: The Widow's Confession
chapters.summary: Mrs. O'Shea, POV. Pressed by guilt after the storm, the widow admits the smuggling ring fed half the village through the blockade years — and that Tomas kept the true ledger as insurance. She begs Petra to burn it. Emotional beat: shame transformed into solidarity; the revelation that survival itself was the crime.

chapters.title: Insurance Against the Living
chapters.summary: Petra, POV. Petra decodes the hidden entries fully: names, payments, and one entry implicating a local magistrate now helping Quill's inquiry. The ledger cuts both ways — it could hang the village or expose the powerful. Nell catches her mother burning a practice page and demands the truth. Emotional beat: power passing unwillingly to the keeper of records.

chapters.title: Nell Runs the Numbers
chapters.summary: Nell, POV. Nell, who has secretly taught herself the code, reconstructs the missing pages and realizes her father died the same week the last shipment vanished. She confronts Petra with the timeline. Mother and daughter argue about truth versus mercy. Emotional beat: inheritance of a dangerous legacy; love expressed as brutal honesty.

chapters.title: The Magistrate's Visit
chapters.summary: Petra, POV. Magistrate Corrigan arrives uninvited, offering to make the inquiry disappear if Petra surrenders the ledger to him rather than Quill. His menace is velvet. Petra stalls, understanding now why Tomas kept insurance. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into clarity; recognizing the predator behind the protocol.

chapters.title: Second Storm
chapters.summary: Petra, POV. The worst storm of the year strikes; the lamp mechanism cracks mid-night and ships founder on the shoals. Petra and Nell hand-crank the backup lens through the dark hours, the workshop's unfinished repair nearly costing lives. Emotional beat: exhaustion transfigured into resolve; failure witnessed and survived.

chapters.title: Quill's Doubt
chapters.summary: Quill, POV. Quill reviews Corrigan's interference and realizes the inquiry was designed to bury the magistrate's own trail. Torn between career and conscience, he warns Petra obliquely: whatever she decides, decide before the armistice. Emotional beat: two keepers of different lights finding common cause; institutional duty cracking under human weight.

chapters.title: What Can Be Carried
chapters.summary: Petra, POV. Petra sorts the house for what matters — Tomas's coat, Nell's drawings, the ledger. She drafts her testimony three ways: full truth, partial truth, silence. Each version costs someone. A letter from the Admiralty confirms the workshop will be seized when the armistice signs. Emotional beat: the theme made literal; choosing what to carry forward.

chapters.title: The Burning
chapters.summary: Petra, POV. Before dawn, Petra burns the coded pages in the workshop forge, keeping only the honest debts — the flour, the nets, the kindnesses. Mrs. O'Shea stands witness. Nell, watching from the stairs, chooses not to stop her. Emotional beat: destruction as protection; grief finally given something to do.

chapters.title: Corrigan Closes In
chapters.summary: Petra, POV. Corrigan, learning the ledger is gutted, threatens Petra with obstruction charges and moves to seize the workshop immediately, armistice or no. Quill intervenes on procedural grounds, buying days. The village, sensing the stakes, closes ranks around the lighthouse. Emotional beat: siege mentality hardening into courage; a community weaponizing its silence.

chapters.title: Armistice Eve
chapters.summary: Nell, POV. Rumors fly that signing comes at dawn. Nell finishes the lens repair beside her mother, their hands working in wordless rhythm — reconciliation without apology. Quill tells Petra privately that Corrigan's superiors are already circling him. Emotional beat: tenderness under deadline pressure; work as the language of forgiveness.

chapters.title: The Inquiry
chapters.summary: Petra, POV. Quill takes Petra's formal statement. She testifies to the debts, the storms, the light kept burning — and to nothing else, because the evidence no longer exists and Quill declines to press. Corrigan erupts; Quill files his report naming Corrigan instead. Emotional beat: testimony as authorship; Petra writing herself into the record on her own terms.

chapters.title: The Signing
chapters.summary: Petra, POV. Bells announce the armistice. The requisition order dies unsigned, and the workshop stands. Corrigan is recalled under investigation; Quill departs with a handshake and an unspoken pact. The village gathers at the lighthouse as the light turns for the first time in peacetime. Emotional beat: release after long tension; joy shadowed by all that was burned to reach it.

chapters.title: A New Ledger
chapters.summary: Petra, POV. Petra opens a fresh book and writes the first entry: not a debt, but a gift — bread sent to Quill's train, oil for the O'Shea lamp. She and Nell walk the shore where the crates once hid. Emotional beat: transformation of accounting into grace; identity rebuilt page by page.

chapters.title: Keeper of the Light
chapters.summary: Petra, POV. One year later, the great storms return but find them ready. Petra signs the official register 'P. Halloran, Keeper,' then adds, in the margin, the names of everyone who helped hold the light. Nell begins her own first entry. Emotional beat: belonging fully claimed; memory carried not as burden but as inheritance.
